# Searchlight vs Elasticsearch benchmark: sample

Generated by `slbench report` from a run started 2026-10-04T12:00:00Z and finished 2026-10-04T12:42:00Z (42m0s). The JSON artifact of the same run holds every number below; compare runs with it, not with this page.

## Spec section 1 targets

| # | Area | Target | Searchlight | Elasticsearch | Status | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | Bulk indexing throughput (docs/s per node) | ≥ Elasticsearch, at equal durability (acknowledged = durable) | 50k docs/s | 30k docs/s | **PASS** | bulk_index: 1.67× Elasticsearch. |
| T2 | Filter / boolean search latency, p50 and p99 | ≤ Elasticsearch | p50 400 µs–1.1 ms, p99 900 µs–3 ms | p50 800 µs–1 ms, p99 2 ms–2.5 ms | **FAIL** | 1 of 2 workloads at or under Elasticsearch on both p50 and p99. Behind: filter_contains (p50 1.1 ms vs 1 ms, p99 3 ms vs 2.5 ms). |
| T3 | Sorted and paged search, p50 and p99 | ≤ Elasticsearch | p50 1.5 ms, p99 4 ms | p50 2.5 ms, p99 6 ms | **PASS** | 1 of 1 workloads at or under Elasticsearch on both p50 and p99. |
| T4 | Aggregation latency (terms, range, histogram, stats) | ≤ Elasticsearch | p50 3 ms, p99 6 ms | p50 5 ms, p99 9 ms | **PASS** | 1 of 1 workloads at or under Elasticsearch on both p50 and p99. |
| T5 | Percolation throughput (docs/s against 10k / 100k saved queries) | ≥ 10× Elasticsearch's percolator, with p99 per document < 1 ms at 100k queries | 10k: 40k docs/s; 100k: 40k docs/s; p99/doc @100k: 700 µs | 10k: 2000 docs/s; 100k: 2000 docs/s; p99/doc @100k: 20 ms | **PASS** | percolate_batch_10000: 20.00× Elasticsearch. percolate_batch_100000: 20.00× Elasticsearch. |
| T6 | Index size on disk and resident memory per million documents | ≤ Elasticsearch | disk 900 MiB/M, RSS 700 MiB/M | disk 1.17 GiB/M, RSS 600 MiB/M | **FAIL** | disk_per_million: 0.75× Elasticsearch. rss_per_million: 1.17× Elasticsearch. |
| T7 | Write-to-visible latency | ≤ 1 s by default (the refresh interval), for both plain writes and refresh=wait_for | visible p50 600 ms p99 1.05 s; wait_for p50 500 ms p99 1 s | visible p50 550 ms p99 1.02 s; wait_for p50 500 ms p99 990 ms | **PASS** | Absolute target (p99 ≤ 1.1 s: the 1 s interval plus poll granularity) for both plain writes and refresh=wait_for. |
| T8 | New replica from zero to serving (10M docs) | ≤ Elasticsearch peer recovery |  |  | **NOT MEASURED** | No recovery workload ran: it needs a Postgres or MySQL store for a second Searchlight node (slbench run --sl-bin with --recovery-store-url). |
| T9 | Node restart to serving | seconds, not proportional to index size (segments are reopened, not rebuilt) |  |  | **NOT MEASURED** | No restart ran: slbench restarts a node it runs itself (--sl-bin), or one --sl-restart-cmd restarts. |
| T10 | Replica failure | no lost acknowledged write, no client-visible error with ≥ 2 replicas |  |  | **NOT MEASURED** | A correctness property under failure, checked by the chaos suite (test/chaos, .github/workflows/chaos.yml), not a performance workload. |
| T11 | Scale | larger than RAM per node (memory-mapped segments), many nodes through shards |  |  | **NOT MEASURED** | Needs a dataset larger than the host's RAM (slbench gen --docs 10000000 on a small host) and the cluster for many nodes. |

## Dataset

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Documents | 1000000 scrape-bot-shaped product listings, 18 fields |
| Seed | 1 |
| File | `products-1m.ndjson` (870 MiB, 912 bytes per document) |
| Saved-search sets | 1k, 10k, 100k |
| Shards | 1 |

Fields: title and description (text, about 60 Zipfian words), brand (2,000 values), category (300), tags (keyword list from 1,000, 1–6 per listing), source (20), condition, sku, url, price (log-normal), list_price, rating, reviews, stock (numbers), in_stock and on_sale (bools), first_seen and updated_at (dates). Values are Zipfian; optional fields are missing from some listings.

## Method

- Each search workload runs 100 warmup then 1000 measured requests, closed loop at concurrency 1, cycling through 64 query variants. Latencies are client-side wall time per request, recorded in an HDR-style histogram (0.1% precision).
- Bulk loads send 1000 documents per request at concurrency 4. Percolation batches hold 100 documents at concurrency 4. Deep paging walks to depth 10000.
- The mixed workload runs for 30 s.
- Every query is written once in Searchlight's DSL and translated to Elasticsearch's by `bench/es` (see the caveats); both engines receive the same sequence.

## Refresh to searchable

Each measured write first sleeps a random, unmeasured delay uniform on [0, refresh interval) — seeded and identical for both engines at the same iteration — so writes land at a random point in the refresh cycle instead of, as a closed loop otherwise would, right after the previous one's own refresh. `refresh_visible`: one document written without refresh, then polled (every 10 ms) until a search finds it; latency runs from the write's start (after its delay). `refresh_wait_for`: the write's own latency with `refresh=wait_for` (also after its delay), then an immediate search must find it.

| workload | engine | load | ops/s | docs/s | p50 | p99 (± run-to-run) | p99.9 | max | errors | SL vs ES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| refresh_visible | searchlight | c=1 | 1 | — | 600 ms | 1.05 s | n/a (n=1000) | 2.1 s | 0 | p50 1.09× |
| refresh_visible | elasticsearch | c=1 | 1 | — | 550 ms | 1.02 s | n/a (n=1000) | 2.04 s | 0 |  |
| refresh_wait_for | searchlight | c=1 | 1 | — | 500 ms | 1 s | n/a (n=1000) | 2 s | 0 | p50 1.00× |
| refresh_wait_for | elasticsearch | c=1 | 1 | — | 500 ms | 990 ms | n/a (n=1000) | 1.98 s | 0 |  |

## Percolation

Saved-search sets are prefixes of one generated stream. `percolate_batch_N`: batches of documents at a fixed concurrency (docs/s, latency per batch). `percolate_single_N`: one document per request (per-document latency). `bulk_percolate`: Searchlight's `_bulk?percolate=true` against Elasticsearch's `_bulk` then percolate.

## Translation caveats

Every place where the engines' semantics differ, or where the Elasticsearch side had a choice of structure, and what the benchmark does about it.

| area | difference | choice | effect on the benchmark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text normalization | Searchlight folds text with Python's str.casefold (ß→ss, ligatures, Cherokee), its str.isspace whitespace set, and NFKC before words; Elasticsearch's lowercase filter is Java's per-code-point toLowerCase and stock Elasticsearch has no NFKC or case folding without the ICU plugin. | A custom normalizer: two pattern_replace char filters (trim, then fold runs of Python's whitespace set to one space) and lowercase. It equals Searchlight on every ASCII text and on all whitespace. | Generated data is ASCII, so the normalizations agree exactly; the cross-check would flag any disagreement. |
| eq, ne, in, starts_with on keyword and text | None for ASCII: both compare the whole normalized value. | term / terms / prefix on the normalized keyword (the field itself); ne is bool.must_not, which like Searchlight matches documents missing the field. | Exact. |

## Notes

## Reproduce

On a Linux host with Docker: `make build`, `go run ./bench/cmd/slbench gen`, start Elasticsearch with `docker compose -f bench/docker-compose.es.yml up -d`, then `slbench run --sl-bin bin/searchlight` (it runs the binary itself; `--recovery-store-url` adds the recovery workload on Postgres) and `slbench report` (`slbench help` lists every flag). `.github/workflows/bench.yml` runs exactly these steps.
